description: Deterministic mapping from legacy RUACH (dynamoai) curriculum IDs to the canonical three-domain curriculum introduced in Release 1.1.
rules: Module mappings are authoritative; lesson mappings inherit the module rule.
Legacy lessons map to their canonical MODULE, not to individual canonical lessons (granularity differs).
Unresolved legacy records must be preserved verbatim and surfaced for manual review; they must never be silently discarded or force-mapped.
Applying this mapping must be idempotent: re-running must not create duplicate completion records.

00.note: Legacy "AI Engineering Foundations" covers AI framing plus programming basics; maps to Programming Foundations and feeds sf.05 computational thinking. Manual review recommended.

01.note: Python for AI Engineers -> Python Foundations.

02.note: Backend Engineering -> API and Backend Foundations (sf.04). Overlaps sf.02 (Software Engineering Foundations) and sf.03 (Tools and Workflow) in areas such as Git, testing and HTTP workflows; see exceptions.

08.note: Model Context Protocol -> ai.08 (MCP / context management).

12.note: Final Capstone has no canonical AI Engineering module; it is preserved but not auto-mapped. Flagged for manual review; see exceptions.

exceptions.issue: Overlaps canonical sf.02 (Software Engineering Foundations) and sf.03 (Engineering Tools and Workflow) which have no dedicated legacy counterpart.
exceptions.resolution: Map to sf.04 as primary; sf.02/sf.03 completion is NOT inferred and must be completed through the canonical experience.

exceptions.issue: Final Capstone has no canonical AI Engineering module.
exceptions.resolution: Preserved verbatim in lesson_mappings with domain=null. No progress awarded. Manual review decides awarding ai.11 or a future capstone module.

exceptions.issue: Legacy lesson ids (e.g. "0.01") are not unique across module namespaces once de-duplicated.
exceptions.resolution: Mappings key on (legacy_module, legacy_id) pairs. Consumers must not treat legacy lesson ids as globally unique.
